anchor_comparisons.concrete_comparison: The approved L1 task uses a 5x5x3 pile with four directly exposed diamonds, a limited pick, and visible lava/support hazards, but its real work is depth-sorted camera rotation and frontmost-face ray selection. Collision Chimes difficulty 1 has a smaller 5x5 2D board, two generated arrows, and eight beats; it adds a short temporal/collision dependency but has no 3D occlusion, hazard, or running motor control. Collision Chimes is therefore not automatically L1 just because its first profile is short, and it is materially different from the approved low-end anchor.

anchor_comparisons.concrete_comparison: The approved L2 task is a one-object active-vision search: cursor proximity reveals one shape, decoys and noise can mislead, and one click within an accepted radius passes. Collision Chimes requires configuring multiple arrows, observing a multi-beat run, and matching an exact wall/slot/beat ledger whose later events depend on earlier turns. Even difficulty 1 Collision Chimes has more persistent state and planning than this one-shot search; the L4 baseline is clearly above the L2 anchor.

anchor_comparisons.concrete_comparison: The approved L3 task requires continuously steering a momentum-bearing ball through three ordered lamps around three walls and wells, with a 50 ms replayed physics tick and full analog drag at the approved baseline. Collision Chimes has less continuous motor control because all edits are before the film, but its five arrows jointly produce an exact 18-beat target and collision turns alter later events. That is a credible step above the L3 board in discrete inverse planning while remaining less state-reactive than a higher physical-control task.

anchor_comparisons.concrete_comparison: The approved L4 task is an 18x11 warehouse with five face gates and a generated path of at least 48 rolls; every roll changes die orientation, which is hidden except at the initial state and sparse scanners. Collision Chimes L4 instead shows the complete target wall ledger, configures five arrows once, and runs 18 beats with no mid-film action. It has a substantial coupled inverse-planning problem but less hidden state and shorter action execution than Blind Dice, so the L4 placement is comparable rather than evidence for L5.

anchor_comparisons.concrete_comparison: The approved L5 task requires four valid adjacent swaps on a 5x5 board. Every accepted swap changes the board, refill cursor, future matches, score, and available next decisions; the exact score and untouched licorice are checked by replay. Collision Chimes L5 increases generated arrows to seven and the film to 24 beats, but all decisions still happen before the run, the target is fully visible, and film state does not change the edit inventory or available controls. Its longer coupled simulation is therefore below the changing-board dependency of the L5 anchor.

visible_baseline_solution.description: A screenshot-only agent first reads the visible TARGET WALL LEDGER, which lists every target beat, wall side, and slot, and the visible rule card describing one-square motion, wall reversal, clockwise turns on occupied or duplicate destinations, and simultaneous beat decisions. In the full baseline it drags the visible brass seed arrow onto empty 9x9 squares; each new arrow starts up, and clicking a placed arrow cycles its direction. It chooses up to six cells, normally configuring the five generated arrows, then starts the film or uses STEP ONE BEAT. During the 18-beat run it watches the moving cells, wall flashes, beat counter, and observed ledger, compares that ledger with the target, and uses REVISE STARTING ARROWS to change the initial configuration before another run. After a complete run it checks the sequence.
visible_baseline_solution.dependent_state: The relevant planning dependency is real but front-loaded: an early wall reversal or arrow encounter changes a direction, and that changed direction affects later positions and wall events. There is no input opportunity during a running film, so the agent is not steering a live object. The agent can observe one beat at a time, retain the visible ledger, revise, and retry.
visible_baseline_solution.precision_and_recovery: The agent must hit exact grid squares and cycle each arrow to the intended direction. The grader accepts an equivalent configuration rather than requiring the hidden generated solution, and the UI provides clear/revise controls. A failed authoritative submission returns a fresh board, while a normal screenshot-only solution can use visible trial films before submission.
visible_baseline_solution.success_condition: The exported payload must contain a valid mode-specific edit transcript, canonical final cells within max_cells, all requested beats, a wall-event transcript that agrees with replay, and an exact canonical match to the visible target sequence. The Python verifier loads the exported result and invokes the same independent collision grader.

baseline_judgment.rationale: The resolver materializes exactly the approved L4/full parameters, and the implementation supports a meaningful L4-style discrete planning problem: five interacting arrows on a 9x9 board, an 18-beat exact event ledger, and later consequences from collision turns. The task is more stateful than Cursor-Controlled Constellation Hunt L2 and plausibly above Gyroscopic Tilt Board L3 in inverse multi-object planning, while Blind Dice Courier L4 supplies a comparable reference with stronger hidden-state/path demands. Exact-Change Candy Cascade L5 is harder in a different way because every accepted decision changes the future board and legal options; Collision Chimes does not. The source supports keeping L4 as a provisional baseline, not an empirical absolute calibration.

findings.claim: The stated minimum event, wall, beat, and collision richness is not guaranteed for every generated seed.
findings.causal_explanation: The normal search accepts a candidate only after _quality and _collision_count pass, but after 6000 misses _find_candidate returns a perimeter fallback and simulates it without rechecking any minimum. The target contract keeps only grid_size, beats, beat_ms, max_cells, and target_events, and the grader never enforces the minimum_* values. A fallback instance can therefore be materially poorer than its profile description while still being gradable.

evidence.explanation: Normal candidate acceptance checks minimum events, distinct walls, distinct beats, and distinct wall/slot pairs.
The fallback after 6000 attempts returns without the quality or collision checks.
The public contract does not carry the minimum richness parameters.
The grader validates only the contract fields and target shape, not minimum event/wall/beat/collision thresholds.

findings.recommended_action: Have the parent quantify fallback frequency across the prescribed multi-seed generation check; if reachable, make the fallback satisfy the active filters or fail generation rather than silently weakening the profile.

findings.claim: The beat_ms decrease is not, by source, an independent increase in configuration difficulty.
findings.causal_explanation: beat_ms schedules the automatic film and bounds the wall-flash timeout, but edit controls are disabled while running and the visible STEP ONE BEAT control advances the same simulation synchronously. An agent can observe each state at its own pace, and the target and revise control remain available before the next submission. The interval may affect observation convenience in an automatic run, but it does not create an expiring correct edit.

evidence.explanation: Automatic scheduling uses beat_ms while stepFilm advances one beat directly and supports the same observation.
Edit controls are available only in edit phase; the step control is available until completion.
The task notes explicitly state that delayed correct edits do not expire.

findings.recommended_action: Treat beat_ms as an observation/presentation parameter in profile rationale; do not credit its numeric decrease as a major difficulty increment unless later calibration shows agents cannot use the step control effectively.

findings.claim: solution_cells describes the generated hidden witness, not a required number of arrows in an accepted screenshot-only solution.
findings.causal_explanation: The generator records solution_cells in the selected random candidate, but the visible contract exposes only max_cells. The grader reconstructs whatever edit transcript the agent submits, checks only the max_cells upper bound, and accepts any configuration whose wall ledger matches the target. The implementation deliberately permits equivalent configurations, so increases in solution_cells do not guarantee a minimum number of simultaneous arrows or a minimum search depth.

evidence.explanation: solution_cells controls how many random cells are used to synthesize the target candidate.

concise_summary: Keep Collision Chimes at the approved L4/full baseline provisionally. Its five-arrow, 18-beat coupled event inversion is above the low anchors and comparable to L4 references, while its fully visible target and pre-film revision loop keep it below the changing-board L5 anchor.
